question: ABCD is a trapezium in which BC || AD and AC = CD. If ∠ABC = 13º and ∠BAC = 164º, then what is the measure of ∠ACD?
solution:
**Given:**

BC || AD

AC = CD

∠ABC = 13º

∠BAC = 164º

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180º

If AC = CD, then ∠CAD = ∠ACD

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5968d86b42904809c36da1ea6be9bd3d0743afc39da81cc44dc9c4abe1747aa0.png] 

In △ABC:

∠ACB = 180º − (164º + 13º)

⇒ ∠ACB = 180º − 177º = 3º

Also AD II BC and AC acts as transversal line so,

∠CAD = ∠ACB = 3° (Alternate interior angles)

In △ACD (AC = CD):

∠CAD = ∠CDA = 3°

∠CAD + ∠CDA + ∠ACD = 180° (Angle sum property)

3° + 3° + ∠ACD = 180°

∠ACD = 180° - 6°

∠ACD = 174°

**∴ ∠ACD = 174º.**

43
